historical_record.description: Concrete retaining wall 15 to 20 feet tall along Broadway, probably by the mason Joseph H. Demerest, who lived on the site from 1863.

Frank W. "Pop" Demerest, the "Hermit of Russian Hill", moved into a cistern here two weeks after the 1906 fire and kept cheap quarters for generations of Bohemians; the compound was cleared in the mid-1950s.
The painter Maynard Dixon and the photographer Dorothea Lange lived in a cottage in Demerest's compound on this site after their marriage in 1920.
Six-unit condominium apartment building designed by Bruce E. Heiser, built on top of the old Demerest wall.
